Brief finds AI in agriculture outpacing federal policy response

AI is being applied across every segment of the food system, from genetic seed selection to optical food safety inspection.

Industry ReleaseSeptember 9, 2026

schedule3 Min Read

Getty Images

The Council for Agricultural Science and Technology has released AI in Agriculture: Transforming the Food System from Data to Decisions to Action, a new peer-reviewed policy brief examining how artificial intelligence is already reshaping American food and agriculture, helping researchers, farmers and food companies improve efficiency, strengthen resilience, conserve resources and deliver a safer food supply. Yet federal policy is not keeping pace.

The brief was authored by Alex Thomasson, professor and director of the Agricultural Autonomy Institute at Mississippi State University, and synthesizes current peer-reviewed research to assess where AI adoption stands today, where it is headed, and what gaps in federal policy, infrastructure and workforce development must be addressed to realize its full potential.

"Artificial intelligence has advanced so fast that it's not really just a research tool anymore; it's embedded in agricultural practice now," said Thomasson. "From autonomous weed spraying to AI-assisted seed selection to real-time food safety inspection on processing lines, the technology is already changing how farmers work, how food moves through the system, and what we expect from that system. The policy conversation needs to catch up."

Related:Lessons learned from regenerative agriculture adoption

The brief identifies five key findings.

AI is no longer a future promise: it is in active use across crop production, animal agriculture, and food supply chains, creating benefits for farmers and consumers, but also creating new policy questions.

AI is evolving from a data analysis tool to a system that takes physical action — what the brief terms "physical AI" — with autonomous machinery and robotics increasingly moving from demonstration to commercial deployment.

Data quantity and quality are foundational to AI performance, making rural data infrastructure a critical policy priority.

AI is being applied across every segment of the food system, from genetic seed selection to optical food safety inspection.

Fifth, federal policy decisions on data centers, rural broadband, data ownership, and workforce development play a role in how AI benefits American agriculture and whether rural communities capture the economic gains of AI locally.

"How AI develops, how it is used in agriculture, and who has access to it over time are going to be heavily influenced by policy decisions, many of which are made by legislators," Thomasson said. "We need funds for research, we need broadband connectivity in rural areas, we need clarity around data ownership, and we need to invest in the workforce that can build and maintain these systems. None of that happens without policy."

Related:MDA accepting applications for sustainable agriculture grant

Chris Boomsma, executive director of CAST, said the brief reflects the organization's core mission of making agricultural science accessible to policymakers.

"CAST exists to translate agricultural science into policy-relevant guidance, and AI in agriculture is exactly the kind of complex, fast-moving topic where evidence-based analysis matters most," said Boomsma. "This brief gives Congress and federal agencies the scientific foundation they need to make smart decisions right now, not after the technology has outpaced the regulatory environment entirely."

The brief is available for download here.

CAST will host a free public webinar on Sept. 14 at noon CT, during which Thomasson will present the brief's key findings and take questions. Registration is available here.

translationZh:
美国农业科学与技术委员会（CAST）发布了题为《农业中的人工智能：从数据到决策再到行动，转型食品系统》的新同行评审政策简报，审视了人工智能如何已在重塑美国食品和农业，帮助研究人员、农民和食品公司提高效率、增强韧性、节约资源并提供更安全的食品供应。然而，联邦政策并未跟上步伐。

该简报由密西西比州立大学农业自主研究所教授兼主任Alex Thomasson撰写，综合了当前同行评审研究，评估AI采用的现状、发展方向，以及为实现其全部潜力必须解决的联邦政策、基础设施和劳动力发展方面的差距。

Thomasson表示：“人工智能发展如此之快，它已不再仅仅是一个研究工具；它现在已经嵌入农业实践之中。从自主除草喷洒到AI辅助选种，再到加工线上的实时食品安全检测，这项技术已经在改变农民的工作方式、食品在系统中的流动方式，以及我们对这个系统的期望。政策讨论需要跟上。”

**相关阅读：再生农业采用的经验教训**

该简报确定了五项关键发现。

第一，AI不再是未来的承诺：它已在作物生产、动物农业和食品供应链中积极使用，为农民和消费者创造利益，但也带来新的政策问题。

第二，AI正从数据分析工具演变为采取物理行动的系统——简报称之为“物理AI”——自主机械和机器人正日益从演示走向商业部署。

第三，数据数量和质量是AI性能的基础，使农村数据基础设施成为关键政策优先事项。

第四，AI正被应用于食品系统的每一个环节，从基因选种到光学食品安全检测。

第五，联邦关于数据中心、农村宽带、数据所有权和劳动力发展的政策决定，影响着AI如何惠及美国农业，以及农村社区能否在当地获得AI的经济收益。

Thomasson说：“AI如何发展、如何在农业中使用，以及随着时间的推移谁能够使用它，将在很大程度上受到政策决定的影响，其中许多决定由立法者做出。我们需要研究资金，需要农村地区的宽带连接，需要明确数据所有权，需要投资于能够建设和维护这些系统的劳动力。没有政策，这些都无从实现。”

**相关阅读：MDA接受可持续农业拨款申请**

CAST执行主任Chris Boomsma表示，该简报反映了该组织让农业科学对政策制定者可及的核心使命。

Boomsma说：“CAST的存在就是将农业科学转化为与政策相关的指导，而农业中的AI正是那种复杂、快速发展的议题，基于证据的分析最为重要。这份简报为国会和联邦机构提供了他们现在就需要做出明智决策的科学基础，而不是等到技术完全超越监管环境之后。”

该简报可在此处下载。

CAST将于9月14日中部时间中午举办免费公开网络研讨会，届时Thomasson将介绍简报的关键发现并回答问题。可在此处注册。
